== widgets.toml
# Herd widgets: one worker per ready GitHub issue in acme/widgets.
# Written by `loopherd init`; yours to edit. loopherd changes it only on a yes to `loopherd herd upgrade`.
repo = "<root>/widgets"
args = ["--permission-mode", "auto"]

[queue]
templates = ["issue", "wayfinding"]
# Prints "<template> <number> <type> <skill> <slug>" per open issue labelled
# ready-for-agent and none of blocked, needs-info, ready-for-human, oldest
# first, matching labels whatever their case.
# $types maps a label to the branch type (else feat); a skill:<name> label
# names the skill the worker builds with (else tdd).
# A wayfinding:research, wayfinding:domain or wayfinding:prototype label
# routes the issue to the wayfinding template, as type docs with the research,
# domain-modeling or prototype skill; any other issue goes to issue.
source = '''
GH_TOKEN=$(gh auth token --user acme) gh issue list --repo acme/widgets --state open --label ready-for-agent --limit 1000 --json number,title,labels --jq '
  {"bug": "fix", "documentation": "docs"} as $types
  | sort_by(.number)[]
  | [.labels[].name | ascii_downcase] as $labels
  | select(any($labels[]; . == "blocked" or . == "needs-info" or . == "ready-for-human") | not)
  | ([$labels[] | $types[.] | values][0] // "feat") as $type
  | ([$labels[] | select(startswith("skill:")) | ltrimstr("skill:") | select(test("^[a-z0-9._:-]+$"))][0] // "tdd") as $skill
  | ([$labels[] | {"wayfinding:research": "research", "wayfinding:domain": "domain-modeling", "wayfinding:prototype": "prototype"}[.] | values][0]) as $wayfinding
  | ([.title | ascii_downcase | scan("[a-z0-9]+")][:5] | join("-")) as $slug
  | "\(if $wayfinding then "wayfinding \(.number) docs \($wayfinding)" else "issue \(.number) \($type) \($skill)" end) \(if $slug == "" then "issue" else $slug end)"'
'''
# Prints "<number> <title>" per open issue the source leaves out, but for
# blocked ones, oldest first, matching labels whatever their case. Ones waiting
# on the human stay, ready-for-agent or not: they are what a dry queue forgets.
backlog = '''
GH_TOKEN=$(gh auth token --user acme) gh issue list --repo acme/widgets --state open --limit 1000 --json number,title,labels --jq '
  sort_by(.number)[]
  | [.labels[].name | ascii_downcase] as $labels
  | select(any($labels[]; . == "blocked") | not)
  | select(any($labels[]; . == "ready-for-agent") | not
      or any($labels[]; . == "needs-info" or . == "ready-for-human"))
  | "\(.number) \(.title)"'
'''
max = 3

[template.issue]
params = ["number", "type", "skill", "slug"]
name = "{herd}-{number}"
branch = "{type}/{number}-{slug}"
done = "GH_TOKEN=$(gh auth token --user acme) gh issue view {number} --repo acme/widgets --json state --jq .state | grep -qx CLOSED"
merged = "GH_TOKEN=$(gh auth token --user acme) gh pr list --repo acme/widgets --head {branch} --state merged --json number --jq 'length > 0' | grep -qx true"
prompt = '''
You're {name}, working GitHub issue #{number} of acme/widgets on branch
{branch} in {worktree}.

Run every gh command as acme, prefixed with
`GH_TOKEN=$(gh auth token --user acme)` as in the commands below.

1. Read the issue and every comment:
   `GH_TOKEN=$(gh auth token --user acme) gh issue view {number} --repo acme/widgets --comments`.
2. Claim it: `GH_TOKEN=$(gh auth token --user acme) gh issue comment {number} --repo acme/widgets --body "claimed by {name}"`,
   then `GH_TOKEN=$(gh auth token --user acme) gh issue edit {number} --repo acme/widgets --add-assignee acme`.
3. Build it with the {skill} skill.
4. Before calling it done, run each check and fix what fails:
   - `cargo test`
   - `cargo fmt --check`
5. Push the branch as acme:
   `GH_TOKEN=$(gh auth token --user acme) git -c credential.helper= -c credential.helper='!gh auth git-credential' push -u origin HEAD`.
   Open a PR with `GH_TOKEN=$(gh auth token --user acme) gh pr create --repo acme/widgets --base main --head {branch} --assignee acme --title "<title>" --body "<summary>"`,
   the body ending with the line `Closes #{number}`.
6. Finish with `loopherd report --kind done "<PR link and one-line summary>"`.

If main moves under you, merge origin/main into your branch; never
rebase or force-push.

If you hit a question only the human can answer, stop rather than guess:
`GH_TOKEN=$(gh auth token --user acme) gh issue edit {number} --repo acme/widgets --add-label needs-info`, comment the
question and the options you see on the issue, then
`loopherd report --kind question "<the exact question>"`.
'''

[template.wayfinding]
params = ["number", "type", "skill", "slug"]
name = "{herd}-research-{number}"
branch = "docs/{number}-{slug}"
done = "GH_TOKEN=$(gh auth token --user acme) gh issue view {number} --repo acme/widgets --json state --jq .state | grep -qx CLOSED"
merged = "GH_TOKEN=$(gh auth token --user acme) gh pr list --repo acme/widgets --head {branch} --state merged --json number --jq 'length > 0' | grep -qx true"
prompt = '''
You're {name}, resolving GitHub issue #{number} of acme/widgets on branch
{branch} in {worktree}. It's a wayfinding task: its output is a research note,
a decision record or a prototype, not a feature.

Run every gh command as acme, prefixed with
`GH_TOKEN=$(gh auth token --user acme)` as in the commands below.

1. Read the issue and every comment:
   `GH_TOKEN=$(gh auth token --user acme) gh issue view {number} --repo acme/widgets --comments`.
2. Claim it: `GH_TOKEN=$(gh auth token --user acme) gh issue comment {number} --repo acme/widgets --body "claimed by {name}"`,
   then `GH_TOKEN=$(gh auth token --user acme) gh issue edit {number} --repo acme/widgets --add-assignee acme`.
3. Resolve it with the {skill} skill.
4. Commit its output (a research note, a decision record or a prototype) on {branch}.
5. Push the branch as acme:
   `GH_TOKEN=$(gh auth token --user acme) git -c credential.helper= -c credential.helper='!gh auth git-credential' push -u origin HEAD`.
   Open a PR with `GH_TOKEN=$(gh auth token --user acme) gh pr create --repo acme/widgets --base main --head {branch} --assignee acme --title "<title>" --body "<summary>"`,
   the body a three-line summary of the outcome, then the line `Closes #{number}`.
6. Finish with `loopherd report --kind done "<PR link and one-line summary>"`.

If main moves under you, merge origin/main into your branch; never
rebase or force-push.

If you hit a question only the human can answer, stop rather than guess:
`GH_TOKEN=$(gh auth token --user acme) gh issue edit {number} --repo acme/widgets --add-label needs-info`, comment the
question and the options you see on the issue, then
`loopherd report --kind question "<the exact question>"`.
'''

# A grill the shepherd starts live with the human: `loopherd add --no-focus
# widgets grill <number> <slug>`, then `loopherd tell` its background, then
# focus. Attended, so feed never spawns it: keep it out of [queue].
[template.grill]
params = ["number", "slug"]
attended = true
name = "{herd}-grill-{number}"
branch = "docs/{number}-{slug}"
done = "GH_TOKEN=$(gh auth token --user acme) gh issue view {number} --repo acme/widgets --json state --jq .state | grep -qx CLOSED"
merged = "GH_TOKEN=$(gh auth token --user acme) gh pr list --repo acme/widgets --head {branch} --state merged --json number --jq 'length > 0' | grep -qx true"
prompt_file = "widgets-grill.md"

[lead]
prompt_file = "widgets-lead.md"
# From [lead_defaults] when init ran. Off means the lead asks the human.
merge = false
install = false
rebase = false
new_cards = false
design_escalation = false
blocked_dialogs = false
follow_ups_ready = false
merge_guard = "hook"
== widgets-lead.md
You're {name}, the lead of herd {herd}, in {worktree}, a detached checkout of
acme/widgets you never commit in. No human is in this pane.

Read `loopherd --skill` in full, its Lead section most closely. Tasks are GitHub issues in acme/widgets. A worker opens a PR whose body carries `Closes #<n>`, so its issue closes when the PR merges.
Run every gh command as acme, prefixed with
`GH_TOKEN=$(gh auth token --user acme)`. You run the shepherd's loop for {herd}'s workers: feed, watch, verify
each worker's PR with a reviewer subagent, send only blocking findings back
to the member, and the after-merge steps.

Your switches (off means the human does it; ask with a question report):
{switches}

Your review-round limit: {review_rounds}.

Grilling is always the human's.

Start now:
1. `loopherd status` and `loopherd reports --all`, to see where the herd is.
2. `loopherd feed {herd} --dry-run`, then `loopherd feed {herd}` if it reads right.
3. Arm `loopherd watch {herd} --timeout 3600` as a background task, and
   re-arm after every exit but `{herd} drained`: on that, report done and
   stop. On `<member> merged`, run `loopherd feed {herd}`,
   which retires it once its issue is closed. On `<name> claimable`, feed.
   Exit 2 is your heartbeat: check each worker's PR for a merge and run
   `loopherd feed {herd} --dry-run`.

When you need the human, run `loopherd report --kind question "<the exact
question>"` and end your turn. With merge off, a merge question carries the PR
link, any PR that must merge first, and the line
`! GH_TOKEN=$(gh auth token --user acme) gh pr merge <n> --repo acme/widgets --merge --match-head-commit <full sha>`
for the head your reviewer verified. Single-quote that question ('...', not
"..."): double quotes run the $(...) and leak the token.
== AGENTS.md
# Agent instructions

## loopherd

A loopherd herd works this repo's ready issues, one worker per issue on its
own branch. A worker reads `docs/agents/loopherd.md` for how to claim, build,
check, hand in and report an issue, and `docs/agents/issue-tracker.md` for
the tracker.
== docs/agents/issue-tracker.md
# Issue tracker: GitHub

Issues and specs for this repo live in its GitHub Issues. Use the `gh` CLI for every
operation.

## Conventions

- **Create an issue**: `gh issue create --title "..." --body "..."`, with a heredoc for a multi-line body.
- **Read an issue**: `gh issue view <number> --json number,title,body,labels,comments`.
- **List issues**: `gh issue list --state open --json number,title,body,labels,comments --jq '[.[] | {number, title, body, labels: [.labels[].name], comments: [.comments[].body]}]'`, narrowed with `--label` and `--state`.
- **Make an issue a sub-issue of a parent**: create it with `gh issue create --parent <parent> ...`, or attach it later with `gh issue edit <parent> --add-sub-issue <child>` (needs `gh` 2.94 or newer). With an older `gh`, call `gh api --method POST repos/<owner>/<repo>/issues/<parent>/sub_issues -F sub_issue_id=<child-db-id>`, passing the child's database id as described under **Blocking**. A repo without sub-issues marks the child with a `Part of #<parent>` first line in its body.
- **Comment on an issue**: `gh issue comment <number> --body "..."`.
- **Apply / remove labels**: `gh issue edit <number> --add-label "..."` / `--remove-label "..."`.
- **Close**: `gh issue close <number> --comment "..."`.

Inside a clone, `gh` finds the repo from `git remote -v` on its own.

## Pull requests as a triage surface

**PRs as a request surface: no.** _(Change to `yes` if external PRs count as feature requests here; `/triage` reads this flag.)_

With the flag at `yes`, PRs take the same labels and states as issues, through `gh pr`:

- **Read a PR**: `gh pr view <number> --comments`, plus `gh pr diff <number>` for the change itself.
- **List external PRs for triage**: `gh api --paginate 'repos/{owner}/{repo}/pulls?state=open' --jq '.[] | select(.author_association | IN("OWNER","MEMBER","COLLABORATOR") | not) | {number, title, author: .user.login, author_association, labels: [.labels[].name]}'`.
- **Comment / label / close**: `gh pr comment`, `gh pr edit --add-label` / `--remove-label`, `gh pr close`.

Issues and PRs draw from one sequence of numbers, so `#42` alone could be either: try `gh pr view 42` first, then `gh issue view 42`.

## When a skill says "publish to the issue tracker"

Create a GitHub issue.

## When a skill says "fetch the relevant ticket"

Read it as in **Read an issue** above.

## Wayfinding operations

`/wayfinder` works through these. Its **map** is one issue, and each ticket is a **child** issue of it.

- **Map**: one issue labelled `wayfinder:map`, whose body holds the Notes, Decisions-so-far and Fog sections. Create it with `gh issue create --label wayfinder:map`.
- **Child ticket**: an issue attached to the map as a sub-issue (see **Make an issue a sub-issue of a parent**). In a repo without sub-issues, list the child in a task list in the map's body and start the child's body with `Part of #<map>`. Label it `wayfinder:<type>`, one of `research`, `prototype`, `grilling` or `task`. A claimed ticket is assigned to the developer driving it.
- **Blocking**: use GitHub's native issue dependencies, which the UI shows. Record that `<blocker>` blocks `<child>` with `gh api --method POST repos/<owner>/<repo>/issues/<child>/dependencies/blocked_by -F issue_id=<blocker-db-id>`. The id is the blocker's numeric database id from `gh api repos/<owner>/<repo>/issues/<n> --jq .id`; neither the `#number` nor the `node_id` works. `issue_dependencies_summary.blocked_by` counts only blockers still open, so it is the live gate. Without dependencies, start the child's body with `Blocked by: #<n>, #<n>`. A ticket unblocks once all its blockers are closed.
- **Frontier query**: take the map's open children (`gh issue list --state open`, limited to the map's sub-issues or task list), drop any that has an assignee or an open blocker (`issue_dependencies_summary.blocked_by > 0`, or an open issue on its `Blocked by` line), and pick the first left in map order.
- **Claim**: `gh issue edit <n> --add-assignee @me`, before any other write in the session.
- **Resolve**: comment the answer with `gh issue comment <n> --body "<answer>"`, close it with `gh issue close <n>`, then add a pointer (a one-line gist and a link) to the map's Decisions-so-far.

## Wayfinding tasks

A ready issue labelled `wayfinding:research`, `wayfinding:domain` or
`wayfinding:prototype` is answered rather than built. loopherd's queue routes
it to the herd's wayfinding template, whose worker resolves it with the
`research`, `domain-modeling` or `prototype` skill and opens a PR with the
output (a research note, a decision record or a prototype) on a `docs/` branch.
These are not `/wayfinder`'s `wayfinder:` labels, which loopherd doesn't route.
== docs/agents/triage-labels.md
# Triage Labels

The skills speak in five canonical triage roles. This file maps each role to
the label string this repo's issue tracker uses.

| Label in mattpocock/skills | Label in our tracker | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `needs-triage` | `needs-triage` | Maintainer needs to evaluate this issue |
| `needs-info` | `needs-info` | Waiting on reporter for more information |
| `ready-for-agent` | `ready-for-agent` | Fully specified, ready for an AFK agent |
| `ready-for-human` | `ready-for-human` | Requires human implementation |
| `wontfix` | `wontfix` | Will not be actioned |

When a skill mentions a role, use the corresponding label string from this
table. Edit the "Label in our tracker" column to match the labels you use.
== docs/agents/loopherd.md
# Working an issue in a loopherd herd

loopherd starts one worker per ready issue, each in its own worktree on its
own branch. The worker's prompt names the issue, the branch and the exact
commands; this doc says what each step is for. How the tracker works is in
`docs/agents/issue-tracker.md`.

## Claiming

Read the issue and every comment first. Then comment `claimed by <member>`
on it, with your member name, and assign it to acme, the account every
gh command runs as. An issue someone else has claimed isn't yours.

## Branch names

`<type>/<number>-<slug>`: the type comes from the issue's labels through the
herd file's type map (by default `fix` for `bug`, `docs` for
`documentation`, else `feat`); the slug comes from the title.
loopherd creates the branch and its worktree; work only there. If main
moves under you, merge `origin/main` into your branch; never rebase or
force-push.

## Checks

Before calling the work done, run each check and fix what fails:

- `cargo test`
- `cargo fmt --check`

## The pull request

Push the branch and open a PR with `--base main`. End its body with the
line `Closes #<number>`, so merging the PR closes the issue; loopherd counts
the issue done once it is closed.

## Stopping on a question

When only the human can answer, stop rather than guess: add the
`needs-info` label to the issue, comment the question and the options you
see, then report it.

## Reporting

Tell the shepherd how the work ended:

- Done: `loopherd report --kind done "<PR link and one-line summary>"`.
- Stopped on a question: `loopherd report --kind question "<the exact question>"`.

## Wayfinding tasks

A ready issue labelled `wayfinding:research`, `wayfinding:domain` or
`wayfinding:prototype` is answered rather than built. loopherd's queue routes
it to the herd's wayfinding template, whose worker resolves it with the
`research`, `domain-modeling` or `prototype` skill and opens a PR with the
output (a research note, a decision record or a prototype) on a `docs/` branch.
These are not `/wayfinder`'s `wayfinder:` labels, which loopherd doesn't route.
